title: Frobenius Borel thickening: quotient and restriction of induced functions
statement:
Let $F$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure], of prime characteristic $p>0$, and let $S$ be a semisimple simply connected $F$-group scheme [def-sc-group-scheme]. Semisimple means smooth, affine, connected and of finite type, with no nontrivial smooth connected solvable normal subgroup, where solvable means that the successive commutator subgroup schemes eventually become trivial. Simply connected means that every surjective homomorphism $S'\to S$ from a semisimple group scheme with finite central kernel is an isomorphism; finite means finite-dimensional coordinate algebra and central means commuting with every element after every scalar extension. A split torus is a group scheme isomorphic to $\mathbf G_m^r$ for some $r\ge0$, where $\mathbf G_m(A)=A^\times$; a maximal torus is one not contained in a larger torus. A Borel subgroup is a maximal smooth connected solvable closed subgroup. Fix a split maximal torus $T\subseteq S$ and a Borel subgroup $B\supseteq T$. For this pair, let $\Phi^+$ be the positive roots given by the nonzero characters of the adjoint action of $T$ on $\operatorname{Lie}(B)$, where $\operatorname{Lie}(B)$ is the kernel of $B(F[\varepsilon]/(\varepsilon^2))\to B(F)$, with its tangent-space structure. A character is a group-scheme homomorphism $T\to\mathbf G_m$; addition of characters means multiplication of their values. Fix an integer $r\ge1$ and write $q=p^r$. If $C=F[S]$, define $S^{(q)}=\operatorname{Spec}(C\otimes_{F,a\mapsto a^q}F)$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]; its group operations are obtained by this base change. The relative Frobenius $F^r_{S/F}:S\to S^{(q)}$ has coordinate map $c\otimes a\mapsto ac^q$. Let $T^{(q)}\subseteq S^{(q)}$ be the base change of $T$, let $S_r=\ker F^r_{S/F}$, and define the closed subgroup schemes $L_r=(F^r_{S/F})^{-1}(T^{(q)})$ and $P_r=B\cap L_r$, with scheme-theoretic inverse image and intersection. Use the notation $S_rT=L_r$ and $B_rT=P_r$. Let $B^{(q)}$ be the base change of $B$ and set $H_r=(F^r_{S/F})^{-1}(B^{(q)})$. There is a proper geometrically integral $F$-scheme $Q_q=S^{(q)}/B^{(q)}$, where geometrically integral means nonempty, reduced and irreducible after every field extension. The composite $\pi_q:S\xrightarrow{F^r_{S/F}}S^{(q)}\to Q_q$ represents the fppf quotient by right multiplication by $H_r$: it is faithfully flat and quasi-compact, and $S\times_FH_r\to S\times_{Q_q}S$, $(g,h)\mapsto(g,gh)$, is an isomorphism. Here the fppf quotient means the sheafification of the right-coset functor for coverings by flat locally finitely presented morphisms with jointly surjective images; in particular an $H_r$-invariant morphism from $S$ to an $F$-scheme factors uniquely through $\pi_q$.
For every character $\chi:B\to\mathbf G_m$, put
$$I_{H_r}(\chi)=\{f\in F[H_r]:f(hb)=\chi(b)^{-1}f(h)\},\qquad I_{L_r}(\chi)=\{f\in F[L_r]:f(la)=\chi(a)^{-1}f(l)\},$$
where $h\in H_r(D)$, $b\in B(D)$, $l\in L_r(D)$, $a\in P_r(D)$ and every equality is required after every commutative $F$-algebra extension $D$. Restriction along $L_r\hookrightarrow H_r$ is an $F$-linear isomorphism $I_{H_r}(\chi)\xrightarrow{\sim}I_{L_r}(\chi)$, equivariant for left translation by $L_r$. A rational action here means a coassociative counital coordinate-algebra coaction; equivariance is equality of coactions. The trivial group and $p=2$ are included.

source.place: Sections 2.3--2.5, printed pp.320--323: rational-function induction, transitivity and the quotient G/G_rB identified with the Frobenius-twisted flag scheme; root-coordinate description before equations (4)--(5). The restriction from H_r to L_r is the corresponding subgroup-product descent statement, supplied in this explicit form by the agent. The local paper is WANTED; read the primary PDF online.

proof.text: The semisimple group $S$ is smooth, connected, affine and of finite type, and $B$ is a maximal smooth connected solvable closed subgroup. Since $F$ is algebraically closed, $\sigma:a\mapsto a^q$ is an automorphism of $F$: injectivity holds in any field and surjectivity follows by taking a root of $X^q-a$. Base change along $\sigma$ is an equivalence of $F$-schemes, inverse to base change along $\sigma^{-1}$, and the projection $X^{(q)}\to X$ is an isomorphism of schemes; it commutes with products, group laws, closed subgroups and commutator subgroups, so it preserves smoothness, connectedness, affineness, finite type, solvability and maximality. Thus $S^{(q)}$ is a smooth connected affine $F$-group of finite type, in particular separated, and $B^{(q)}$ is a maximal smooth connected solvable closed subgroup. Apply [lem-sfb-algebraic-group-homogeneous-quotient] to $B^{(q)}\subseteq S^{(q)}$: it gives a separated finite-type $F$-scheme $Q_q$ and $p_q:S^{(q)}\to Q_q$, flat, surjective, locally of finite presentation and quasi-compact, with $p_q(g)=p_q(g')$ exactly when $g^{-1}g'\in B^{(q)}$ on points over every $F$-scheme, and with fpqc local lifts of all points. Hence $(g,b)\mapsto(g,gb)$ is a well-defined map $S^{(q)}\times_FB^{(q)}\to S^{(q)}\times_{Q_q}S^{(q)}$, and on points over every test scheme it is bijective with inverse $(g,g')\mapsto(g,g^{-1}g')$; by Yoneda it is an isomorphism of schemes, so $p_q$ is a faithfully flat right $B^{(q)}$-torsor and a singleton fppf covering. Apply [lem-sfb-borel-quotient-proper-geometry] with $G=S^{(q)}$, $H=B^{(q)}$ and $p=p_q$: $Q_q$ is geometrically integral, and, since $B^{(q)}$ is maximal among smooth connected solvable closed subgroups, $Q_q$ is proper over $F$.

source.place: Section 2.5, printed pp.321--322, X=G/B and its Frobenius twist; geometry supplied by Milne and the cited existing quotient nodes.

proof.text: Write $\varphi=F^r_{S/F}$. By [lem-sfb-smooth-connected-group-frobenius-flat], $\varphi$ is finite and fppf. Composing the two singleton fppf covers using [lem-sfb-space-fppf-covering-calculus](3),(4) makes $\pi_q=p_q\varphi$ fppf. It is quasi-compact: for affine $V\subseteq Q_q$, cover $p_q^{-1}(V)$ by finitely many affine opens; their inverse images under the finite, hence affine, map $\varphi$ are affine and cover $\pi_q^{-1}(V)$. On every test algebra, the torsor identity for $p_q$ from step 1 gives $\pi_q(g)=\pi_q(g')$ exactly when $\varphi(g)^{-1}\varphi(g')\in B^{(q)}$, exactly when $g^{-1}g'\in H_r$. The two morphisms $(g,h)\mapsto(g,gh)$ and $(g,g')\mapsto(g,g^{-1}g')$ are inverse, giving $S\times H_r\simeq S\times_{Q_q}S$ scheme-theoretically. Base changing the fppf cover $\pi_q$ gives local lifts of every point of $Q_q$, so this identity identifies the fppf sheafification of right cosets with $Q_q$. Moreover an invariant morphism $u:S\to Z$ has equal pullbacks to this kernel pair. By [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-representable-descent] (the cover is fpqc by [lem-trf-fppf-covering-is-fpqc]) it descends uniquely to $Q_q\to Z$. The descended map is over $F$ by uniqueness applied to the two structural composites.

source.place: Section 2.5, printed p.322, equation (3), G/G_rB identified with the twisted flag scheme; descent expanded using Stacks 023Q.

proof.text:
Apply [lem-sfb-smooth-connected-group-frobenius-flat] also to $B$, which is smooth connected affine of finite type by the Borel hypothesis. Form $W=H_r\times_{B^{(q)},\varphi|_{H_r},F^r_{B/F}}B$. The singleton family $F^r_{B/F}$ is an fppf, hence fpqc, covering by [lem-trf-fppf-covering-is-fpqc], so the projection $v:W\to H_r$ is an fpqc covering by [lem-galois-fpqc-covering-base-change]. For a pair $(h,b)$ of test-algebra points of $W$, $\varphi(h)=\varphi(b)$, so $l=hb^{-1}\in S_r\subseteq L_r$ and $h=lb$. This defines a morphism $W\to L_r\times B$. Given $f\in I_{L_r}(\chi)$, the expression $g_0(h,b)=\chi(b)^{-1}f(hb^{-1})$ is a regular function on $W$: it is the product of the pullback of $f$ with the invertible regular function $\chi(b)^{-1}$. On $W\times_{H_r}W$, write the two coordinates as $(h,b),(h,b')$ and put $l=hb^{-1}$, $l'=hb'^{-1}$, $a=bb'^{-1}$. Then $a\in B_r\subseteq P_r$ and $l'=la$. Hence
$$\chi(b')^{-1}f(l')=\chi(b')^{-1}\chi(bb'^{-1})^{-1}f(l)=\chi(b)^{-1}f(l).$$
The equality is an identity of morphisms, verified on every test algebra; it therefore includes nilpotent elements. By [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-representable-descent] with target $\mathbf A^1_F$, $g_0$ descends uniquely to a regular function $g$ on $H_r$. Its structural map is over $F$ by uniqueness.

source.place: Section 2.3, printed p.320, equation (1) (covariant functions); Section 2.5, p.322 (Frobenius kernels). Agent subgroup-product descent argument, not a claimed quotation from Kaneda.

proof.text: For $c\in B(D)$ the map $(h,b)\mapsto(hc,bc)$ sends $W$ to $W$ over right multiplication on $H_r$, because $\varphi(hc)=\varphi(bc)$. Since $hc(bc)^{-1}=hb^{-1}$, the defining formula gives $g_0(hc,bc)=\chi(c)^{-1}g_0(h,b)$. Pull back along the fpqc cover $W\times B\to H_r\times B$ and use uniqueness in [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-representable-descent] to obtain $g(hc)=\chi(c)^{-1}g(h)$ as a morphism identity. Thus $g\in I_{H_r}(\chi)$. On the base change $W\times_{H_r}L_r\to L_r$, the condition $h\in L_r$ forces $\varphi(b)=\varphi(h)\in T^{(q)}$, hence $b\in P_r$. Covariance of $f$ yields $f(hb^{-1})=\chi(b)f(h)$, so $g_0(h,b)=f(h)$; the same descent uniqueness gives $g|_{L_r}=f$. These covers are fpqc by [lem-galois-fpqc-covering-base-change].

source.place: Section 2.3, printed p.320, equations (1),(3); explicit inverse to restriction, with covariance and restriction checked by Stacks 023Q.

proof.text: Restriction takes $I_{H_r}(\chi)$ into $I_{L_r}(\chi)$ because $P_r\subseteq B$. Conversely, if $g\in I_{H_r}(\chi)$ and $f=g|_{L_r}$, then on $W$ one has $g(h)=g(lb)=\chi(b)^{-1}f(l)=g_0(h,b)$. Uniqueness in [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-representable-descent] shows that the construction above recovers $g$. Restriction is therefore bijective and is $F$-linear by restriction of regular functions. The covariance subspaces are stable under left translation since left and right multiplication commute. For every commutative $F$-algebra $D$ and $a,l\in L_r(D)$, restriction commutes with left translation by the identity $((a\cdot g)|_{L_r})(l)=g(a^{-1}l)=(a\cdot(g|_{L_r}))(l)$. This is the identity of regular action morphisms, equivalently of coordinate coactions, so the isomorphism has the required rational $L_r$-equivariance. If $S=1$, both spaces are $F$ and restriction is the identity. No argument divides by $2$ or assumes reduced test algebras.
